mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (below 1.5%) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced interest rates lower the discount rate for equity valuations and stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 4.5% signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes economic slowdowns and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, reflecting stronger economic fundamentals and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, which typically triggers central bank tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by more than 100k and UNRATE declines by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS increases.
